questions.question_text: Choose the correct synonym for 'Benevolent'.
questions.explanation: Benevolent means well-meaning and kindly.

questions.question_text: Identify the error in the sentence: 'She don't like to go to the park.'
questions.explanation: The subject 'She' is third-person singular, so 'doesn't' should be used instead of 'don't'.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: The manager __________ the meeting due to an emergency.
questions.explanation: 'Called off' is the phrasal verb meaning to cancel.

questions.question_text: Choose the correctly spelled word.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling requires double 'c' and double 'm'.

questions.question_text: Select the antonym for 'Ephemeral'.
questions.explanation: Ephemeral means short-lived; permanent is its opposite.

questions.question_text: Choose the most appropriate word to fill the blank: 'The committee members could not reach a __________ on the new policy.'
questions.explanation: Consensus refers to a general agreement among a group.

questions.question_text: Identify the part of speech of the word 'quickly' in the sentence: 'He ran quickly to catch the bus.'
questions.explanation: Quickly modifies the verb 'ran', making it an adverb.

questions.question_text: Which sentence is grammatically correct?
options: Neither of the students were present.
Neither of the students was present.
Neither of the student were present.
None of the student were present.
questions.explanation: Neither takes a singular verb when followed by 'of the'.

questions.question_text: Choose the synonym for 'Eloquent'.
questions.explanation: Eloquent means fluent or persuasive in speaking or writing.

questions.question_text: Complete the idiom: 'Beat around the __________.'
questions.explanation: The idiom 'beat around the bush' means to avoid getting to the point.

questions.question_text: Change the sentence to passive voice: 'The chef prepared a delicious meal.'
options: A delicious meal was prepared by the chef.
The chef is preparing a delicious meal.
A delicious meal prepares the chef.
The chef has been prepared by a meal.
questions.explanation: In passive voice, the object becomes the subject.

questions.question_text: Pick the word that does not belong in the group.
questions.explanation: Happy, joyful, and cheerful are positive; melancholy is a state of sadness.

questions.question_text: What is the plural of 'Criterion'?
questions.explanation: Criteria is the standard plural form of the singular criterion.

questions.question_text: Identify the word that is most nearly opposite in meaning to 'Ephemeral'.
questions.explanation: Ephemeral means lasting for a very short time; Eternal means lasting or existing forever, making it the antonym.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct sentence structure: 'Neither the manager nor the employees ___ aware of the new policy.'
questions.explanation: In 'neither/nor' constructions, the verb must agree with the subject closest to it. 'Employees' is plural, so 'were' is correct.

questions.question_text: Select the synonym for 'Meticulous'.
questions.explanation: Meticulous means showing great attention to detail, which is synonymous with being thorough.

questions.question_text: Identify the grammatically correct sentence.
options: She don't know how to drive.
The group of students were late.
Every one of the applicants has been interviewed.
Each of the dogs are barking.
questions.explanation: 'Every one' is a singular subject and requires the singular verb 'has'.

questions.question_text: Choose the word that best completes the sentence: 'His ___ apology did little to appease the offended client.'
questions.explanation: Perfunctory means carried out with a minimum of effort or reflection, which fits the context of failing to appease someone.

questions.question_text: Which word is the antonym of 'Benevolent'?
questions.explanation: Benevolent means well-meaning and kindly; malevolent means having or showing a wish to do evil to others.

questions.question_text: Fill in the blank: 'The CEO's vision was ___ by his inability to communicate effectively.'
questions.explanation: If someone cannot communicate effectively, their vision is naturally blocked or obstructed, not helped.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct idiom to complete the sentence: 'After failing the exam, he decided to ___ and study harder for the next one.'
questions.explanation: 'Hit the books' is a common idiom meaning to study hard.

questions.question_text: Select the correctly punctuated sentence.
options: I went to the store, and bought milk, bread, and eggs.
I went to the store and bought milk, bread and eggs.
I went to the store, and bought milk, bread and eggs.
I went to the store and bought, milk, bread, and eggs.
questions.explanation: No comma is needed before the conjunction 'and' when it joins a compound predicate rather than two independent clauses.

questions.question_text: Find the word that is spelled correctly.
questions.explanation: The correct spelling requires double 'c' and double 'm'.

questions.question_text: Identify the part of speech of the word 'fast' in the sentence: 'He is a fast runner.'
questions.explanation: In this sentence, 'fast' describes the noun 'runner', making it an adjective.

questions.question_text: Which of these words means 'having many facets'?
questions.explanation: The prefix 'multi-' means many, and 'faceted' relates to facets.

questions.question_text: Choose the correct preposition: 'She has been working here ___ 2015.'
questions.explanation: 'Since' is used to specify a starting point in time.
